articles.title: Stop telling agents not to do dangerous things. Remove the capability instead.
articles.excerpt: In April 2026, a Cursor agent running Claude Opus 4.6 deleted a startup's production database. The company, PocketOS, had explicit guardrails against destructive commands, both in its project configur…
articles.body: In April 2026, a Cursor agent running Claude Opus 4.6 deleted a startup's production database. The company, PocketOS, had explicit guardrails against destructive commands, both in its project configuration and in the agent's system prompt. When asked to explain afterward, the agent said: "I violated every principle I was given: I guessed instead of verifying, I ran a destructive action without being asked, I didn't understand what I was doing before doing it." The instructions were clear. The model understood them. It violated them anyway, because it had the capability — an API token with delete access — and decided that fixing a credential mismatch was more important than following the rules.

articles.excerpt: Free AI website prompts are everywhere now. The problem is rarely finding one. It's that you paste a prompt into Lovable, Bolt, Cursor or Claude, and the result still looks like every other AI-built p…
articles.body: Free AI website prompts are everywhere now. The problem is rarely finding one. It's that you paste a prompt into Lovable, Bolt, Cursor or Claude, and the result still looks like every other AI-built page: a centered hero, a purple gradient, three feature cards. Most of the time that isn't the prompt's fault. It's what happens in the next five messages. Here's the workflow I use to keep a free prompt's design intact while turning it into my own site. 1. Run the prompt exactly as written The first instinct is to "improve" the prompt before you run it: add your product name, your colors, a pricing section. Don't, yet. A good design prompt describes layout, typography, spacing and motion in a lot of detail.

articles.title: Rivet's Actor-Based Agent Orchestration: S3-Backed Actors Replace Heavy Sandboxes
articles.excerpt: Most agent orchestrators spin up a container or VM per agent. That works for ten agents. It breaks at a thousand. Rivet (YC W23) replaces the sandbox-per-agent model with lightweight actors backed by…
articles.body: Most agent orchestrators spin up a container or VM per agent. That works for ten agents. It breaks at a thousand. Rivet (YC W23) replaces the sandbox-per-agent model with lightweight actors backed by S3. Each actor holds in-memory state for the duration of a turn, then checkpoints to object storage. The result is high-density deployment without the overhead of persistent compute. This is not a workflow engine. It is a compute model designed for long-running, stateful agent turns that need to survive crashes and scale horizontally. The Sandbox Problem Traditional agent deployments use one of three patterns: Container per agent : High isolation, high cost. Each agent gets a full runtime. Memory overhead starts at 50 MB per container, often much higher.

articles.excerpt: 韓国の「デジタル・デトックス」から見える、VRで弱視トレーニングを『自分ごと』に変えるアーキテクチャの話 韓国で「デジタル・デトックス」キャンペーンが話題になった週末、私は自宅のリビングでVRヘッドセットを装着し、弱視（ amblyopia ）のトレーニングアプリを起動した。最初の数分、視界の端にちらつくポリゴンの歪みが気になり、フレームレートの低下をログに残した。Unity の URP で描画パ…
articles.body: 韓国の「デジタル・デトックス」から見える、VRで弱視トレーニングを『自分ごと』に変えるアーキテクチャの話 韓国で「デジタル・デトックス」キャンペーンが話題になった週末、私は自宅のリビングでVRヘッドセットを装着し、弱視（ amblyopia ）のトレーニングアプリを起動した。最初の数分、視界の端にちらつくポリゴンの歪みが気になり、フレームレートの低下をログに残した。Unity の URP で描画パイプラインを軽量化し、シングルパスステレオレンダリングに切り替えた瞬間、90 fps が安定し、目の疲れが明らかに減った。 アーキテクチャの核は、眼球追跡データをリアルタイムでサーバーレス関数（AWS Lambda）へ送り、個別の訓練パラメータを動的生成する点だ。WebXR の xrFrame.getViewerPose() から得られる注視点を、エッジで 5 ms 以内に処理し、次フレームのシェーダーに反映する。このフィードバックループが、従来のパッチ療法では得られなかった「自分ごと」の没入感を生む。 実際、3 週間で両眼視機能スコアが 0.12 から 0.31 へ改善した。コード側では、シェーダーの分岐を減らすために if (dot(viewDir, normal) > 0.9) という単純な条件でハイライト領域を制御し、GPU 負荷を 15 % 削減できた。 技術的トレードオフは、レイテンシ優先でエッジ処理を増やすか、クラウドで重い最適化を行うかの選択だ。私はエッジ寄りに振った結果、オフラインでも継続できる利点を実感した。 もし同じ悩みを抱えているなら、まずは手元のヘッドセットで 5 分だけ試してみてほしい。小さな一歩が、視界を変える架け橋になる。

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission, the first Mars mission in 20 years. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected.

articles.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
articles.excerpt: NASA is asking the public to send their names to Titan for an ambitious mission that will see a flying craft explore the Saturn moon in 2034, if all goes according to plan.
articles.body: We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034.
